h1: Solar Panel Removal and Reinstall Cost: 2026 Price Guide
heroSub: Real numbers for detach and reset in Greeley and Northern Colorado, plus what your roofer's scope and your hail claim should actually cover.
introHtml:
If a roofer just told you the panels have to come off before they can touch your roof, here's the short answer. In 2026, solar detach and reset in the Greeley area runs $200 to $500 per panel, which puts a typical 20-panel home array at around $3,500 for the full job. That covers removal, safe storage while the roof gets replaced, reinstallation, and electrical recommissioning so the system comes back on the way it should.

The good news for hail claims: on a covered roof claim, the detach and reset line item is typically paid by the insurance claim, not out of your pocket. Below you'll find a full price table, the factors that push jobs up or down, and answers to the questions homeowners ask us mid-reroof. Every job gets a free written estimate, so you'll have a firm number before anything comes off the roof.

sections.heading: What a detach and reset actually includes
sections.html:
A proper detach and reset isn't just lifting panels off and setting them back down. The crew documents the array layout, disconnects and labels the wiring, removes panels and racking, and stores everything safely while your roofer works. Once the new roof is on, the racking goes back with new flashing at every penetration, the panels are reinstalled in their original layout, and the system is recommissioned and tested.

Storage during a normal reroof timeline is usually included in the price, and so is the electrical recommissioning at the end. If a quote leaves either of those out, ask what happens when the roofer runs long or the system won't power back up. That's where cheap quotes turn expensive. You can see the full process on our detach and reset service page.

sections.heading: Cost factors: what moves the price up or down
sections.html:
Two 20-panel jobs can land hundreds of dollars apart. Here's what actually drives the difference:

  • Panel count. The biggest factor. More panels means more labor, more racking, and more wiring to disconnect and restore.
  • Roof pitch and height. Steep roofs and two-story homes slow the crew down and require more safety setup, which raises the per-panel rate.
  • Racking condition and type. Older or discontinued racking may need replacement parts. Newer rail systems come off and go back faster.
  • Array layout. One clean rectangle is quicker than panels split across three roof faces with separate wire runs.
  • Electrical setup. Microinverters, optimizers, and older string inverters each take different amounts of work to disconnect and recommission.
  • Timing and access. Emergency callouts after a storm add $150 to $300, and tight lot access or landscaping the crew has to work around can add time.

This is why we do free written estimates instead of quoting blind over the phone. Ten minutes on site gets you a real number, not a range.

sections.heading: Who pays when hail is involved
sections.html:
Here's the part that surprises a lot of Weld and Larimer county homeowners: if your roof replacement is a covered hail claim, the solar detach and reset is typically part of that claim. Adjusters in Northern Colorado see this constantly, and the detach and reset shows up as its own line item on the scope. If it's missing from yours, your roofer or adjuster can add it through a supplement, which is routine paperwork, not a fight.

That usually means your out-of-pocket cost for the solar work is nothing beyond the deductible you're already paying on the roof. Damaged panels are a separate question, since hail can crack cells even when the glass looks fine. If your array took hits, read our guide to solar hail damage or call the 24/7 emergency line if you've got exposed wiring or a system that shut down after the storm.

sections.heading: Detach and reset vs permanent removal
sections.html:
Most homeowners mid-reroof want the panels back on, but not everyone. If your system is old, underperforming, or you're planning to replace it anyway, permanent removal runs $1,500 to $3,000 for a typical home array. That covers taking down the panels and racking, safely decommissioning the electrical, and leaving the roof ready for your roofer with no penetrations left open.

Permanent removal costs less than a detach and reset because there's no storage, no reinstall, and no recommissioning. If you're on the fence, get both numbers in writing and decide once you know what your insurance scope covers. We serve the whole area, from Greeley out to Windsor, Evans, and Johnstown.

faq.q: How much does it cost to remove and reinstall solar panels for a roof replacement?
faq.a: Plan on $200 to $500 per panel in 2026. A small 8 to 12 panel array runs $1,500 to $2,500, a typical 20-panel array lands around $3,500, and large or complex arrays run $6,000 to $8,000 or more. A free written estimate pins down your exact number.

faq.q: Does insurance pay for solar detach and reset on a hail claim?
faq.a: Typically yes. When your roof replacement is a covered hail claim, the detach and reset is normally paid as a line item on that same claim. If it's not on your scope yet, it can usually be added through a supplement, so check your paperwork before paying out of pocket.

faq.q: Is panel storage included while my roof is being replaced?
faq.a: For a normal reroof timeline, yes, storage is usually included in the detach and reset price. If your project is going to stretch for months, tell us up front so we can confirm storage in your written estimate.

faq.q: Who turns the system back on after the panels go back up?
faq.a: We do. Electrical recommissioning is included, which means the wiring is reconnected, the system is tested, and it's producing power before we call the job done. You shouldn't have to chase a second contractor to flip the switch.

faq.q: What does emergency solar service cost after a storm?
faq.a: Storm-damage emergency callouts add $150 to $300 on top of the work itself. That covers getting a crew out fast, any hour, to secure damaged panels, deal with exposed wiring, and make the array safe until the full repair or reset is scheduled.
